I think one of the battles of well-fitting jeans, especially in classic denims, is that we're applying the fit and movement expectations of a wool or cotton smart-casual trouser to a fabric weight and seam construction which was never originally intended to fit that way.  It's a case of "style" and "fit" becoming conflated on a garment type that wasn't historically originally designed to fit, fall, or move in the same way as we now want it to

Most brands (even the "premium" ones) use a good amount of "vanity sizing." My waist is about 31 inches but in virtually every brand, from Levis to Naked and Famous to Iron Heart, I'm a size 28 to 30 at most. Gustin is the one exception I've found, which, for me, is pretty true to size. Also, from my experience, jeans, especially ones with any spandex/stretch, stretch much more over time than they shrink in the wash/dryer. Most of my older pants are at least a size larger on the waist. Obviously you don't want anything cutting off circulation, but if you think your jeans are a little tight, they WILL stretch out in the tight places. This does not apply to shrink to fit or other unsanforized denim, which will shrink considerably in the wash/dryer. TED Talk over.
